## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, gaunt, and thin woman with many angles and no curves. She has dark hair that shows gray streaks, which is worn twisted behind in a hard little knot fastened by two wire hairpins. Over time, her hair has grown grayer and her face noticeably softer, though she frequently appears old, worn, and tired, and is shorter in height than [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md).

## Personality

A woman of rigid conscience, stern devotion to duty, and customary placidity, she maintains a self-contained and reserved exterior that rarely permits displays of deep emotion. She is highly practical, sensible, and determined, often showing a critical nature and becoming sarcastic after headaches or moments of self-betrayal. Deeply neat and unromantic, she detests cats and refuses on principle to criticize ministers in any form. As a famous cook, she is celebrated for her homemade currant wine, matchless plum puffs, and skills in making braided mats to keep her home in order. Driven by her principles, she aims to drill [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) into a tranquil uniformity of disposition while ensuring the girl receives a good education to earn her own living. Furthermore, she refuses to be surpassed by other local housekeepers and privately harbors a hope that [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) will eventually make a match.

## History

Marilla Cuthbert grew up at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), where she spent sixty years leading an easy, conservative life alongside her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md). In her youth, she quarreled with John Blythe and refused to forgive him when he asked, a choice she would later look back on with quiet regret. Her life took a major turn when she and [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, only for a mix-up to bring a young girl, [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) instead. Though initially determined to send the child back, Marilla was moved by pity for Anne's neglected past and agreed to raise her, taking full responsibility for the girl's upbringing and discipline. Over the years, Marilla found her strict principles tested and softened by Anne's imaginative mishaps, growing to love the girl deeply and feeling immense pride as [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) excelled academically. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack, Marilla grieved alongside [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), only to learn shortly after that her own failing eyesight threatened to force the sale of [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). However, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) sacrificed her college scholarship to stay home, teach locally, and care for Marilla. To enable [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to eventually attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), Marilla invited the newly widowed Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) to move into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), and later agreed to permanently raise the orphaned Keith twins, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md). As the years passed, Marilla continued to manage the bustling household, offering a steady home for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) during her holiday breaks and life milestones.

## Quotes

> "No. We want a boy to help Matthew on the farm. A girl would be of no use to us. Take off your hat. I’ll lay it and your bag on the hall table."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P30](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0030)

> "Well, undress as quick as you can and go to bed. I’ll come back in a few minutes for the candle. I daren’t trust you to put it out yourself. You’d likely set the place on fire."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P44](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0044)

> "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P25](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0025)

> “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind P35](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0035)

> "I suppose we could, but we decided not to. Matthew took a fancy to her. And I must say I like her myself—although I admit she has her faults. The house seems a different place already. She’s a real bright little thing."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P9](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0009)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla is the adoptive mother, friend, and mentor of [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md). Though initially shocked by the mix-up that brought a young girl to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) instead of a boy, Marilla decided to keep [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), raising her and instructing her in household duties, religion, and practical skills. Over time, Marilla developed a deep maternal affection and close bond with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), which helped sustain her after the loss of her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md).

### [Martin](../character/martin.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--martin.md)

[Martin](../character/martin.md) works under Marilla's authority at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), taking orders for farm labor and tasks around the property. Marilla directs him in his duties to keep the household and farm functioning, particularly as she manages the property following Matthew's death.

- Commands  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P28](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0028), [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P29](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0029)</sub>

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

[Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) and Marilla are long-time neighbors and close friends who frequently visit one another to discuss community news and practical matters. Despite occasional friction, such as Rachel's blunt criticism of [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) that sparked a household dispute, Marilla trusts Rachel's judgment and regularly seeks her counsel on raising children and managing local affairs.

### [Davy Keith](../character/davy-keith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/davy-keith--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla acts as the guardian and authority figure over [Davy Keith](../character/davy-keith.md), having taken him in alongside his twin sister following their mother's funeral. She finds herself constantly challenged by Davy's mischievous pranks and stubborn behavior, requiring her to enforce strict discipline while working with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to guide his moral development.
